text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

---Stockholm Bourse's managing director Bengt Ryden says that closer cooperation between the Stockholm and Copenhagen stock exchanges is a vital prerequisite for any closer relationship between all Nordic exchanges. Ryden said he did not see any foreign bourses meddling in the setting up of a joint Nordic stock exchange, which he did no envisage happening overnight. Stockholm has Europe's seventh biggest stock exchange.

---Danish transport minister Bjoern Westh insists that the rail tunnel section of the new Great Belt train-car bridge-tunnel fixed link between Denmark's two main islands is the safest in Europe. Westh is to meet Danish Rail and Great Belt management to discuss criticism of the fixed link's security - the link is due to open for goods traffic on April 6 and for rail passenger services in June.

--- Danish institutional investors are calling for higher dividends from local corporations. They maintain that dividends always rise slower than results and that higher dividends would help attract more overseas investors.
---The government is to look into tightening merger rules in Denmark in the light of the current takeover battle for Danish roadbuilder Phoenix involving local firms and Norway's Rieber.

---Danish opposition to joining Europe's economic and moinetary union (EMU) seems to be rising as more voters make up their mind on the issue. A new poll shows 55.6 percent of Danes opposed to EMU, with 33.4 percent in favour and a Danish EU commissioner urges politicians to come out and campaign for Denmark to take part in monetary union.

--The political position of Per Stig Moeller, the Conservative Party's new leader, is weaker despite his survival after trying to hush up revelations of a 30-year-old drunken-driving offence. Moeller's chances of becoming prime minister in any new Conservative-Liberal centre-right coalition are deemed low compared to those of the Liberal leader, former foreign minister Uffe Ellemann-Jensen.
